fact: Spring Valley at Ute Creek's design guidelines, revised May 2026, prefer real turf and allow artificial turf in rear yards only, with ARC approval, when it is a realistic natural green with a UV-protective coating, professionally installed and kept up by the homeowner, densely bladed in varied shades, suited to its use, and should be 1½ to 2 inches high.
quote: Real turf is preferred. Artificial turf may be permitted (in rear yards only) with ARC approval, and must conform to the following minimum standards: Must be realistic (i.e., a “natural green grass” color) and must have an ultraviolet protective coating to prevent color fading in full sun. Must be Professionally Installed and continuously maintained by the homeowner. Must have densely packed blades within the turf’s construction, and vary in green shade to more closely resemble real-life grass appearance. Must be appropriate to the use for which it is intended, as different types of artificial grass serve different functions. Should be at least one and one-half (1½) to two (2) inches high.
source_label: Spring Valley @ Ute Creek Homeowners Association, Design Guidelines and Site Restrictions (revised May 2026), Sec. 2.36 Landscaping
notes: PDF downloaded and read 2026-09-26 (20 pages; cover reads 'Revised: Revised May 2026'). Bullets dropped from the quote. The height line is the only one of the five standards written with 'Should'; the other four say 'Must'. Putting greens are not named anywhere in the guidelines.

fact: The Spring Valley at Ute Creek guidelines require at least 30% vegetation in front yards, ban all-rock front yards, keep artificial turf off walks, front steps and decks, and decide front-yard gravel, terracing and large planters case by case.
quote: Artificial turf is not permitted on walks, front steps, or decks. … Front yards must maintain a minimum of 30% vegetation. To maintain continuity in the neighborhood, NO All-Rock Front Yards will be Permitted. … Gravel, terracing, and large planters are permitted in rear yards. Permission to install gravel, terracing, or large planters in front yards will be determined on a case-by-case basis only.
source_label: Spring Valley @ Ute Creek HOA, Design Guidelines and Site Restrictions (revised May 2026), Secs. 2.25 Entrances (Front) and 2.36 Landscaping
notes: Sec. 2.25 cross-refers to '2.3 Landscaping'; the landscaping section is 2.36 in the May 2026 revision.

fact: Under the Spring Valley at Ute Creek guidelines, flowers, planters, sod, a sprinkler system, gardens, mulch or rock in the rear yard and small bushes under fence height need no ARC approval, while rear plantings that will grow above the fence need approval naming the species.
quote: Rear landscaping that will exceed the fence height (i.e. large trees or shrubs) need ARC approval (specifying the tree species). … Flowers, flowerpots, planters (must not be attached to the home), sod, sprinkler system, gardens, mulch or rock in the rear yards and small bushes under fence height do not need ARC Committee approval.
source_label: Spring Valley @ Ute Creek HOA, Design Guidelines and Site Restrictions (revised May 2026), Sec. 2.36 Landscaping

fact: Spring Valley at Ute Creek permits xeriscaping that follows City of Longmont guidelines, uses at least four design elements, is well designed and maintained, and waters its trees and plants with a hidden drip system.
quote: Xeriscaping or gardenscaping is permitted. Xeriscaping must follow City of Longmont guidelines. Xeriscaping must consist of no less than four (4) design elements (including—but not limited to—trees, small rocks, large rocks or boulders, native flowers and grasses, bushes, mulch, pavers or other stepping stones, wood elements, etc.) and must be well-designed and well-maintained regularly. Xeriscaping and gardenscaping shall make use of a hidden drip irrigation system for any trees or plants.
source_label: Spring Valley @ Ute Creek HOA, Design Guidelines and Site Restrictions (revised May 2026), Sec. 2.36 Landscaping

fact: Spring Valley at Ute Creek landscaping plans go to the ARC before work starts and show fences, decks, sod, seeded areas, retaining walls, rock, the sprinkler plan, nursery sizes and species and a drainage and grading plan, with a timetable; landscaping must be finished within 365 days of plan approval, and the timetable may be extended for weather.
quote: Landscaping plans must be submitted to the ARC prior to commencement of landscaping. Plans must depict fences, decks, sod, seeded areas, retaining walls, rock, railroad ties, sprinkler system plan, sizes and species of nursery material, and include a drainage and grading plan showing any drainage improvements. Other requirements are as follows: Plans must include a timetable for starting and completing the landscape. Landscaping must be complete three hundred sixty five (365) days (One -1 Year) following approval of landscape plans. … Request for extension of the submitted timetable may be permitted for weather-related reasons.
source_label: Spring Valley @ Ute Creek HOA, Design Guidelines and Site Restrictions (revised May 2026), Sec. 2.13.3 Landscaping Plans

fact: Spring Valley's amended declaration requires complete plans approved in writing by the Architectural Review Committee before landscaping or any other improvement goes in, and a submittal the committee has not acted on within 30 days is deemed denied.
quote: fences, walls, exterior lighting, landscaping, or any other improvements shall be constructed, erected, relocated, removed or installed on a Lot, … unless complete plans and specifications shall have been first submitted to and approved in writing by the Architectural Review Committee ("Committee") as may be outlined in the Rules and Regulations. … The Committee shall reply to all submittals of plans made in accordance herewith in writing within 30 days after receipt. In the event the Committee fails to take any action on submitted plans and specifications within 30 days after the Committee has received the plans and specifications, approval shall be deemed to be denied.
source_label: Amended and Restated Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, and Restrictions of Spring Valley (Boulder County Reception No. 03928495, recorded 11/16/2021), Secs. 6.1 Required Approval and 6.6 Reply and Communication

fact: The Spring Valley at Ute Creek guidelines also treat plans not approved or disapproved within 30 days as denied, then add a sentence limiting when deemed approval applies, wording the declaration does not carry.
quote: Failure of the ARC or designated representative to approve or disapprove plans and specifications within thirty (30) days of submittal shall be deemed to be denied. Deemed approval shall only apply when matters specifically and sufficiently described in plans and specifications are submitted to, and received by, the ARC and are in full compliance with the Covenants and Guidelines.
source_label: Spring Valley @ Ute Creek HOA, Design Guidelines and Site Restrictions (revised May 2026), Sec. 2.13.4 Review and ARC Action
notes: Declaration Sec. 6.6 (record arc-approval) says only that no action within 30 days is deemed denial; it has no deemed-approval sentence.

fact: Spring Valley's declaration has owners report finished work within five days and allow an exterior inspection, withdraws approval of work that doesn't match what was approved, revokes an approval not started within six months unless extended, and expects approved work done within six months of starting.
quote: Owners shall notify the Committee of completion of the improvement's installation or construction within five days of such completion; … Upon completion of an improvement, Owners authorize the Committee or its representative(s) to enter onto the Lot for exterior inspection; … If the improvement as built does not conform to the improvement as approved by the Committee, the Committee's approval will be deemed withdrawn, … All improvements approved by the Committee must be commenced within six months from the date of approval. If not commenced within such time, then such approval shall be deemed revoked by the Committee, unless the Committee gives a written extension for commencing the work. Additionally, except with written Committee approval otherwise, … all work approved by the Committee shall be completed within six months of commencement.
source_label: Amended and Restated Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, and Restrictions of Spring Valley (Boulder County Reception No. 03928495), Secs. 6.2(e), (f), (h) and 6.8
notes: Guidelines Sec. 2.13.3 and the Design Review Request form give landscaping one year from approval; the declaration's six-plus-six months is the tighter clock once work starts.

fact: Spring Valley's declaration says the committee's approval may not be unreasonably withheld and lets it ask the applicant to reimburse the board's actual review expense; Flagstaff Management's page for the association posts no design review fee.
quote: The approval or consent of the Committee on matters properly coming before it shall not be unreasonably withheld, and actions taken shall not be arbitrary or capricious. … Upon its review of such plans, specifications and submittals, the Committee may require that the applicant(s) reimburse the Board for actual expense incurred by it in its review and approval process.
source_label: Amended and Restated Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, and Restrictions of Spring Valley (Boulder County Reception No. 03928495), Sec. 6.3 Architectural Criteria
notes: The Flagstaff page (record flagstaff-page) lists a transfer fee but no design review fee; the DRR form names no fee.

fact: Spring Valley at Ute Creek's Design Review Request form has a landscaping box for enclosed plans, restates the committee's 30 days to decide, says approval does not replace City of Longmont permits, and asks for a completion date within 1 year.
quote: ( ) Landscaping (Enclose plans) … I understand that per the Covenants of Spring Valley @ Ute Creek HOA, the committee has 30 days from the receipt date of the request to come to a decision. I understand that this approval does not relieve me of my responsibility to obtain building permits from the City of Longmont, if required. … (Must be completed within 1 year)
source_label: Spring Valley @ Ute Creek, Design Review Request form (c/o Flagstaff Management, Inc., Longmont)

fact: Flagstaff Management's Spring Valley at Ute Creek page says a Design Review Request is required for all improvements and the committee has 30 days to decide, and its architecture and landscape documents list pre-approved roof colors and paint schemes but no pre-approved water-wise garden designs.
quote: Architecture & Landscape PLEASE NOTE: A Design Review Request Form is required to be turned in for all improvements. The committee has 30 days to make a decision, so please plan accordingly. Pre-Approved Roof Colors Pre-Approved Color Schemes View Design Review Request Form & Instructions
source_label: Flagstaff Management, Spring Valley at Ute Creek community page (Architecture & Landscape documents)
notes: Page read 2026-09-26. The quote is the whole Architecture & Landscape list. The same page lists 2026 board meetings on October 13 (budget) and November 5 (annual) and a $350.00 transfer fee; no design review fee is posted.

fact: Spring Valley's amended and restated declaration, recorded in Boulder County on 11/16/2021, covers 279 lots in Spring Valley Phase One First Filing and its Replat A, land Centex Homes first placed under the Spring Valley covenants on March 14, 1997.
quote: 03928495 11/16/2021 … On March 14, 1997, Centex Homes submitted the real property described on Exhibit A to that certain Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, and Restrictions of Spring Valley … The number of Lots currently included in the Community is 279. … Spring Valley Phase One First Filing, Boulder County, Colorado. … Spring Valley Phase One First Filing, Replat A, Boulder County, Colorado.
source_label: Amended and Restated Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, and Restrictions of Spring Valley (Boulder County Reception No. 03928495, recorded 11/16/2021), Recital A, Sec. 2.2 and Exhibit A
notes: Exhibit A: Phase One First Filing Lots 18-22 Block 2, 1-51 Block 5, 1-44 Block 6, 1-29 Block 7, 1-23 Block 8, 1-37 Block 9, 1-11 Block 10, 1-12 Block 11, 1-9 Block 12 (221), and Replat A Lots 1-14 Block 1, 1-19 Block 2, 1-11 Block 3, 1-14 Block 4 (58): 279.

fact: In Boulder County's parcel map, 57 of the 279 Spring Valley at Ute Creek lots share a boundary with the six parcels platted as Spring Valley Golf Course, 41 of them in Block 5 of the first filing and 16 in Block 2 of Replat A.
quote: SubCode 7610 SPRING VALLEY GOLF COURSE - LG: 6 parcels, AcctType EXEMPT (Legal: BLK 1, PT BLK 2, BLK 3, BLK 4 SPRING VALLEY GOLF COURSE) · Exhibit A lots intersecting those parcels: 57 at 0, 1 and 10 feet; 58 at 40 feet · SubCode 7608 Block 5: 41 · SubCode 7611 Block 2: 16

The count holds at 57 from 0 to 10 feet (58 at 40, 62 at 100), so 57 is lots whose lines touch the course parcels. The HOA's own site says the neighborhood borders several holes on Ute Creek's back nine (record hoa-site).

fact: The Spring Valley at Ute Creek HOA's own site says Centex Homes built its 279 homes from the late 1990s, that the neighborhood borders several holes on Ute Creek's back nine, where the creek comes into play on four holes and five lakes and two streams also come into play, that the course has putting and chipping greens, and that open space backs up to many of the homes.
quote: The neighborhood was established in the late 1990's. The homes were built by Centex Homes. There are 279 homes in the Spring Valley at Ute Creek HOA. The neighborhood borders several holes along the back nine of Ute Creek Golf course. The golf course is named after the creek that meanders through the entire layout and comes into play on four holes. There are also five lakes and two streams that come into play, most prominently on the back nine. … Ute Creek at Spring Valley is open for public play and it also offers a driving range with putting and chipping greens. The neighborhood also features an elementary school (Alpine Elementary), a city park (The Rough & Ready Park) and some open space areas backing up to many of the homes in the sub-division.
source_label: Spring Valley at Ute Creek HOA, About Us (springvalleyatutecreek.com)
notes: Page read 2026-09-26. The same page carries a 2021-era note about 2022 meeting dates, so its wording is older than the 2026 guidelines; the lot count matches the declaration.

fact: Spring Valley's declaration puts every lot under a golf ball easement: golfers may retrieve errant balls except inside a fenced or walled yard without the owner's permission; owners are told to expect early and late course maintenance, possible treated-effluent watering and heavy fertilizing at times; and owners must not distract play, including with unfenced or unleashed dogs.
quote: The individual residential properties in Spring Valley shall be subject to an easement which permits golf balls to unintentionally come upon the individual residential properties and to allow golfers the right to retrieve the errant golf balls, provided however, if any individual residential property is fenced or walled, no golfer shall be allowed to seek or retrieve his/her or any other errant golf ball within the interior of the enclosed property without first obtaining the property owner's permission. Each individual residential property owner has been informed that he/she can expect that (a) maintenance activities of the golf course shall begin early in the morning and extend late into the evening; (b) the golf course may be required to use treated effluent watering and during certain periods of the year the golf course will be heavily fertilized; and (c) golf balls are not susceptible of being easily controlled and accordingly may land or strike beyond the golf course boundaries. Further, all property owners shall be obligated to refrain from any action which would detract from the playing qualities of the golf course or unreasonably distract golfers from the play of golf. Such prohibited actions shall include but are not limited to activities such as the playing of loud music or other sounds or noises which would distract the play of golf and the keeping of unfenced or unleashed dogs or other pets which would interfere with the play of golf due to loud barking, running on the golf course, picking up golf balls or other like interference with the play of golf.
source_label: Amended and Restated Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, and Restrictions of Spring Valley (Boulder County Reception No. 03928495), Sec. 2.8 Golf Ball Easement
notes: 'May be required to use treated effluent watering' is the declaration's disclosure, not a finding that the course uses reuse water today; no City source on Ute Creek's irrigation water was found.

fact: Spring Valley's declaration reserves drainage easements across the rear five feet and side five feet of every lot, bars improvements or grading there that change or obstruct the flow through the swales, has owners keep the slope set at final grading, and sends any change to a lot's established drainage to the committee as a plan.
quote: The Association hereby reserves to itself easements for drainage or drainage facilities across the five rear and five side feet of each Unit. No improvements shall be placed or permitted to remain on any Unit nor shall any change in grading be permitted to exist which may change the direction of flow or obstruct or retard the flow of water through channels or swells within such rear and side yard drainage easements. … Each Owner shall maintain the grading upon his Unit at the slope and pitch fixed by the final grading thereof, including landscaping and maintenance of the slopes. … In the event that it is necessary or desirable to change the established drainage over any Unit or other Common Elements which a Unit Owner has a duty to maintain, then the party responsible for the maintenance of such real property shall submit a plan to the Architectural Review Committee for its review and approval.
source_label: Amended and Restated Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, and Restrictions of Spring Valley (Boulder County Reception No. 03928495), Secs. 2.7 Easements for Drainage and Utilities and 5.5 Maintenance of Lots and Improvements

fact: The Spring Valley at Ute Creek guidelines require ARC approval for any change affecting drainage, want landscaping to drain water away from the foundation and driveway, and let the ARC ask for a drainage engineer's report with a landscaping plan.
quote: ARC approval required for any changes affecting drainage. … There can be no interference with the established drainage pattern over any property except as approved in writing by the ARC. When landscaping is installed, it is very important to ensure that water drains away from the foundation and driveways of the house … The ARC may require a report from a drainage engineer as part of the landscaping or improvement plan approval.
source_label: Spring Valley @ Ute Creek HOA, Design Guidelines and Site Restrictions (revised May 2026), Sec. 2.23 Drainage

fact: The Spring Valley at Ute Creek guidelines say ARC approval is no assurance that a project meets government rules or needs no permit, and that owners should not build improvements over utility easements without the utility's consent.
quote: Approval by the ARC will not constitute assurance that improvements comply with applicable governmental requirements or regulations or that a permit or approvals are not also required from applicable governmental bodies. … In making improvements to Property, homeowners are responsible for locating all water, sewer, gas, electrical, cable television, or other utility lines or easements. Homeowners should not construct any improvements over such easements without the consent of the utility involved and homeowners will be responsible for any damage to any utility lines.
source_label: Spring Valley @ Ute Creek HOA, Design Guidelines and Site Restrictions (revised May 2026), Secs. 1.5 Effect of Governmental and Other Regulations and 1.6 Utilities

fact: The Spring Valley at Ute Creek guidelines keep developer-built split-rail fences in place unless the ARC approves a change, allow no front-yard fences or chain link, build fences to the wing or two- or three-rail specifications at 4 or 5 feet, taper six-foot fencing between homes to split-rail height, and let owners add hog wire inside existing split-rail fencing without approval.
quote: Split rail fences installed by the developer can not be removed or replaced without specific approval or waiver from the ARC Committee. … No fencing of any variety or type shall be permitted in the front yard … Fences-provided they are built to wing fence or (3) three or (2) two rail fence specifications and are either 4 (four) or 5 (five) foot height only. … No chain link fences shall be allowed. 6’ (six foot) fencing between homes must taper to split rail height. Wire mesh (also known as “hog wire” or hardware cloth) that conforms to design standards may be installed, without ARC approval, on the inside of existing split-rail fencing. No chicken wire is permitted.
source_label: Spring Valley @ Ute Creek HOA, Design Guidelines and Site Restrictions (revised May 2026), Sec. 2.27 Fences

fact: The Spring Valley at Ute Creek guidelines require conventional fixtures that follow Longmont's dark-sky guidance, cap lamps at the output of a 100-watt incandescent bulb, ask for low landscape lighting to be used sparingly, and call security floodlighting and LED lighting unacceptable.
quote: Must be conventional style with illumination patterns that do not cause a nuisance to neighboring properties. Exterior lighting must adhere to Longmont city guidelines regarding dark sky lighting. Lamps shall not exceed the light output of a 100W incandescent bulb. High wattage commercial/industrial fixtures are unacceptable. Low level landscape or garden lighting should be used sparingly and must not adversely affect adjacent property. Security floodlighting and LED lighting is unacceptable
source_label: Spring Valley @ Ute Creek HOA, Design Guidelines and Site Restrictions (revised May 2026), Sec. 2.38 Lights and Lighting

fact: The Spring Valley at Ute Creek guidelines will not approve a new wood-burning fire pit or chiminea, and approve natural-gas or propane fire pits that meet the HOA's guidelines and Longmont's building code.
quote: A DRR requesting the addition of a Chiminea or wood burning firepit will not be approved. Homeowners completing a DRR asking permission to add firepits using natural gas or propane will be approved if they meet HOA guidelines for architectural improvements and City of Longmont building code.
source_label: Spring Valley @ Ute Creek HOA, Design Guidelines and Site Restrictions (revised May 2026), Sec. 2.28 Firepits, Chimineas and Firewood Storage

fact: The Spring Valley at Ute Creek guidelines require ARC approval for an open patio, which must be part of the landscape plan and not block drainage, while their paving section requires approval for front yards only.
quote: ARC approval required. Patios must be an integral part of the landscape plan and must be located so as not to create an unreasonable level of noise for adjacent property owners. … Must be located so as not to block any existing drainage pattern on lot. … ARC approval for front yards only required regardless of whether for walks, driveways, porches, patio areas, or other purposes and regardless of whether concrete, asphalt, brick, flagstone, stepping stones, precast patterned or exposed aggregate concrete pavers are used as paving material.
source_label: Spring Valley @ Ute Creek HOA, Design Guidelines and Site Restrictions (revised May 2026), Secs. 2.41 Patios (Open) and 2.42 Paving
notes: The two sections pull different ways on a rear patio: 2.41 requires approval for open patios, 2.42 requires approval of paving (patio areas included) in front yards only.

fact: The Spring Valley at Ute Creek guidelines require ARC approval for dog houses, runs and pet enclosures, and allow dog runs only in the rear yard, out of easy view from the street and matched to the home's exterior.
quote: ARC approval required. Needs to be screened from view of street and/or public view and must comply with the City Code. … Dog runs will only be permitted in the rear yard where they will not be readily visible from the street and they must match the exterior of the home (wood, brock, stone etc.).
source_label: Spring Valley @ Ute Creek HOA, Design Guidelines and Site Restrictions (revised May 2026), Sec. 2.21 Dog Houses, Runs and Pet Enclosures

fact: Spring Valley Golf Estates is a separate planned community with its own homeowners association, whose declaration was recorded in Boulder County on 09/12/2000 with 51 lots and a declarant's right to create up to 160.
quote: 2077969 … 09/12/2000 … is Spring Valley Golf Estates. It is a planned community. Section 2.2. The Association: The name of the Association is Spring Valley Golf Estates Homeowners Association, Inc. Section 2.3. Maximum Number of Lots: The Common Interest Community contains 51 Lots. The Declarant reserves the right to create a maximum of 160 Lots.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions for Spring Valley Golf Estates (Boulder County Reception No. 2077969, recorded 09/12/2000), Secs. 2.1 to 2.3
notes: The PDF is a 52-page scan with no text layer; pages 1 and 13 were rendered and read as images 2026-09-26. Flagstaff Management manages both associations (its Communities list names both).

fact: Spring Valley Golf Estates' rules, amended April 24, 2018, require every lot's front and back yards to be at least 50% sod unless its ARC approves otherwise, and require in-ground sprinklers front and back.
quote: Addendum of Section 9.3, sub-section T (1) All front, back and side yards on all Lots must be landscaped including a minimum of fifty percent (50%) sod in both the front and back yards, unless otherwise approved by the (ARC). … (3) An in ground sprinkler system is required in both the front and back yard.
source_label: Spring Valley Golf Estates Homeowners Association, Rules and Regulations (amended April 24, 2018), Addendum to Sec. 9.3.T
notes: Colorado's backyard turf protection for detached homes (co-hoa-backyard-detached, effective 2023) postdates these rules; how the 50% sod minimum is applied to a backyard turf request today was not found in writing.

fact: Spring Valley Golf Estates asks for a Design Review Request at least 30 days before work starts, aims to decide within 30 days, says no reply is not approval, and has the approved form displayed in a front window until the project is done.
quote: The DRR form shall be submitted to ARC at least 30 days prior to the intended initiation of work on the homeowner’s lot. … ARC shall make every effort to review the DRR and approve or disapprove all requests within 30 days after receipt. The failure to receive any communication from Flagstaff Management related to a request does not imply or provide approval of that request. … A copy of approved DRR’s are to be visibly displayed in a window, near the front door. The form must remain in place from the start, until the finish of the project.
source_label: Spring Valley Golf Estates, Design Review Request Guidelines and Form (6-6-16)
